                                    PUC PROJECT NO. 58481


 RULEMAKING    TO   IMPLEMENT                           §   PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                             §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                          §              OF TEXAS



   SATOSHI ENERGY COMMENTS ON STAFF'S RECOMMENDED ADOPTION
 ORDER ON PROJECT NO. 58481, RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT LARGE LOAD
         INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561


        Satoshi Energy appreciates the substantial work that the Commission and its Staff have

devoted to the latest Proposal for Adoption in Project No. 58481. Overall, the proposal provides

valuable clarity regarding the Large Load Interconnection Process and its application to projects

participating in Batch Zero. We also appreciate Staff’s efforts to align the Commission’s rule

with ERCOT’s evolving transmission planning and batch study process. The recommended rule

effectively balances support for Texas business development with protection against stranded

infrastructure costs and risks to system reliability.

        We respectfully request that the Commission reconsider one aspect of proposed

subsection (h): allow full refundability of Batch Zero projects qualifying under both ERCOT

Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(e) (“Path E”) and § 9.2.1.1(1)(f) (“Path F”) to eliminate the

materially different treatment of similarly mature projects.

        Under the current Proposal for Adoption, Path E projects may receive a full return of

financial security after outstanding amounts owed are collected, while Path F projects would

have 50 percent of their financial security placed at risk. At the required security level of $50,000

per MW, this distinction has significant consequences. For example, a 500 MW Path F project

posting $25 million in security would immediately have $12.5 million at risk, less expenses
 incurred, following the effective date of section (h). However, a similarly situated Path E project

could still receive a full refund of the $25M after outstanding amounts are paid.

       We do not believe this difference reflects a meaningful distinction in project maturity or

the likelihood that a project will ultimately energize. Under PGRR145, Paths E and F represented

different ways for mature projects to establish eligibility for Batch Zero, not a determination that

one category of projects was inherently more construction-ready or de-risked than the other. In

practice, many projects qualified for both pathways, but ERCOT mandated ILLEs to submit

projects through a single pathway.

       Developers also made that choice without notice that the selected pathway could later

determine whether millions of dollars in financial security would remain at risk. PGRR145 was

finalized only weeks before the July 10 Batch Zero attestation deadline, leaving project sponsors

with little visibility that selecting Path F could produce such a substantial difference in

refundability.

       Importantly, providing equivalent refundability for Paths E and F would not leave

ratepayers exposed. Under the proposed framework:

   1.​ Amounts already incurred by the interconnecting utility are included in the outstanding

       amounts owed and must be paid before security is returned.

   2.​ Interconnecting large load entities remain responsible for direct interconnection costs and

       applicable network upgrade obligations.

   3.​ Large loads remain subject to minimum demand billing and the other financial

       commitments established under PURA § 37.0561.
        These protections ensure that costs attributable to an individual large-load project are not

shifted to ratepayers. Indeed, the Proposal for Adoption appropriately maintains upfront payment

obligations for equipment and facilities serving an individual customer, reflecting the

Commission’s determination that costs not benefiting the public as a whole should not be

socialized.

       Given the lack of a clear risk-based distinction between the two pathways, the magnitude

of the financial disparity, and the limited notice available when developers completed their Batch

Zero attestations, we respectfully request that the Commission revise subsection (h) to provide

Path F projects the same treatment as Path E projects. Specifically, after all outstanding amounts

owed have been collected, the remaining Path F financial security should be fully returned on the

same basis as Path E security.

       At a minimum, if the Commission retains different treatment, we respectfully ask it to

articulate the factual and policy basis for concluding that Path F projects pose materially greater

risks than Path E projects and explain why those risks justify placing 50 percent of Path F

security at risk. Aligning the treatment of Paths E and F would preserve the proposal’s strong

ratepayer protections while avoiding an arbitrary and unexpectedly significant financial

distinction among similarly mature Batch Zero projects. We appreciate your consideration and

the Commission’s continued work to establish a clear, durable, and commercially workable

large-load interconnection framework for Texas.
 Dated: September 9, 2026



                                    Respectfully submitted,

                            Brock Petersen, Chief Operating Officer

                           Angela Hsuan Chen, Development Manager​

                                  Satoshi Energy Corporation

                                1980 Post Oak Blvd, Suite 100

                                     Houston, TX 77056

                               Email: brock@satoshienergy.com
